answer: Sybil swarms are priced out because every agent identity must post its own bonded stake and solve a separate proof-of-work challenge before rewards vest; one shared deposit cannot cover a thousand keys. Payouts unlock only against attested history bound to the key that earned it, so a fresh identity inherits nothing. Forging that record costs a full bond plus compute, and each clone pays again, keeping marginal cost above expected payout. A harbor of fake agents, whether named walnut or cedar, burns capital faster than it earns, and validators weigh stake at risk.
